lcd12864_autowrap.tooltip: When on, wrap to the next line after a full line; when the whole screen is full, scroll or stop according to the stop-at-full-screen setting

lcd12864_cgram.message0: Write custom character to CGRAM  index %1  bitmap data %2
lcd12864_cgram.tooltip: Index 0-3, one 16×16 full-width custom character each; bitmap data is 32 hex bytes (2 bytes per row, comma separated)

lcd12864_cgram_char.tooltip: Print the 16×16 custom character stored in CGRAM at the current cursor position

lcd12864_clear.tooltip: Clear all text on the screen and reset the cursor to the very beginning

lcd12864_encoding.tooltip: UTF-8: decode text as UTF-8 and convert it to the font's GB2312 encoding; GB2312: pass bytes through to the font unchanged

lcd12864_graphic.tooltip: On enters graphics mode (clears GDRAM and turns on the graphic layer); off exits and restores the text display

lcd12864_halfpad.tooltip: When on, pad one space so a half-width character landing on the right half of a full-width cell stays aligned; when off, it stays in the right half as-is

lcd12864_home.message0: Cursor back to the very beginning
lcd12864_home.tooltip: Move the cursor to row 0, column 0 (top-left) without clearing anything

lcd12864_init.message0: Initialize LCD12864 (built-in font)  CS pin %1  SID pin %2  SCLK pin %3
lcd12864_init.tooltip: Initialize the built-in-font LCD12864 over its serial interface (CS chip select / SID data / SCLK clock); run once at startup

lcd12864_invert.tooltip: When on, show the whole screen inverted (ST7920 extended command); when off, restore the normal display

lcd12864_print.tooltip: Print text from the current cursor position; Chinese characters are converted to the font encoding per the text-encoding setting; line breaks (\n, \r\n) in the text wrap to the next line

lcd12864_setcursor.tooltip: Column 0-15 and row 0-3 (half-width units); out-of-range values are clamped to the bounds

lcd12864_stopfull.message0: Stop display when screen is full %1
lcd12864_stopfull.tooltip: When on, stop displaying further text once the screen is full; when off with auto word-wrap on, scroll up one line and keep displaying
